The core set is also coarser than the vendor's: the adapter maps five vendor values onto three (FILED and RELEASED become accepted, EXAM_HOLD and DOCS_REQUIRED become needs-attention).

FilingStage matches the six ReviewQueue values one for one, with only the Q_ prefix dropped and BROKER_SIGNOFF shortened to sign-off, and shipment.ts branches on every vendor stage. The spec's glossary defines its own sets (clearance state, filing outcome) but never names these review-queue stages, so the distinctions come from the vendor.

The domain glossary names the term "entry disposition" with exactly these five values. It says the customs regulation the broker is licensed under defines the set, and that each value requires a different client action. So the one-for-one mapping in clearwise-filing.gateway.ts exists because the vendor implements the same regulation, not because the domain copies the vendor.

CoverageVerdict is a domain concept. The spec glossary names "coverage verdict" as owned by the domain, with exactly the values covered/prior-auth/not-covered. It is also coarser than ClaimStatus: the adapter maps both PAID and CAPTURED to covered, and refill.ts branches on it to set its own refill states. (REJECTED has no mapping shown, which may be a gap in the adapter.)

The adapter maps each SwitchRoute value one-for-one onto a ClaimPath member (ROUTE_DIRECT→direct, ROUTE_CLEARINGHOUSE→relayed, ROUTE_BATCH→deferred). The spec's glossary doesn't name or need claim paths, so refill.ts is branching on the vendor's switch-routing distinctions under new names.
